title: Autoscaler metrics stitching bug causes unexpected reserved-pool shrinkage and customer-facing shortfalls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A metrics ingestion/stitching regression rolled out with the telemetry pipeline caused per-tenant utilization to be misattributed across reserved vs. burst pools. The autoscaler interpreted the aggregated metrics as sustained low utilization for several reserved pools and initiated scale-downs, which in turn created capacity shortfalls for burst requests. This manifested as increased tail latency and request rejects for affected tenants during a weekend traffic surge.

Why this is unique: Unlike previous warmup/headroom logic bugs, this is a bug in the telemetry aggregation layer: multiple ingestion shards merged the same tenant windows twice due to a recent change in the 'stitching key' normalization. The autoscaler relies on that aggregated metric as a signal for reserve sizing. Because reserved-pool utilization looked lower than reality, the controller reduced headroom and did not honor burst-safe thresholds.

Impact observed:
- Time window: 2026-03-07 23:10 UTC -> 2026-03-08 05:40 UTC (peak customer impact)
- ~12 tenants experienced increased p95 latency and 503s (not all customers escalated)
- Named escalations: AcmeHealth (support ticket #9871), TaskFlow (ticket #9900), EduPilot (ticket #9924) — high-severity production incidents with degraded SLAs for short window
- Autoscaler created 28 scale-down events across 5 reserved pools in US-west-2; 18 of those were unnecessary (reconciled later)

Reproduction steps:
1) Re-run the telemetry ingestion job with the new normalization table and a synthetic tenant producing both reserved and burst traffic patterns (see test harness in repo).
2) Observe duplicated windows in the stitched metrics stream: two samples with identical window_id but different shard_labels are merged without dedupe.
3) Feed the aggregated metrics into the autoscaler simulator -> it computes reserve utilization at ~38% instead of real ~72% and triggers scale-down policy because the grace-state threshold is computed against the observed utilization.

Root cause (technical):
- Change: telemetry normalization patch (PR #10422) introduced removal of the tenant_namespace label during window key construction to canonicalize noisy labels from edge proxies.
- Regression: the normalization produced an identical stitching_key for windows that previously differed by immutable shard_id. The downstream dedup step relied on shard_id to de-duplicate overlapping ingestion batches. With shard_id removed, dedup no longer matched and windows were double-counted in some ingestion paths while being dropped in others — producing both over- and under-counts depending on ingestion timing.
- Autoscaler dependency: the reserve sizing heuristic uses aggregated utilization over the last 5m stitched window; it is not robust to transient duplicate/partial samples and lacks a cross-check against allocator slot counts when deciding to scale down.

Mitigation / hotfix applied (timeline):
- 2026-03-08 02:15 UTC: On-call (Marco) throttled autoscaler scale-down decisions for all reserved pools in us-west-2 (feature-flag: "autoscaler.scale_down.freeze.region.us-west-2").
- 2026-03-08 03:05 UTC: Rolled back telemetry normalization patch (PR #10422) to restore shard_id behavior — ingestion dedupe resumed. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/10422-revert
- 2026-03-08 04:00 UTC: Re-enabled controlled scale-downs with an added conservative safety latch (min_headroom=2 GPUs per reserved pool enforced by the controller).
- 2026-03-08 05:30 UTC: Customer-facing service levels recovered to nominal; follow-up comms sent to impacted tenants.

Fix implemented (in-progress):
- Short-term: Reverted normalization + applied emergency safety latch in autoscaler to prevent headroom dropping below min_headroom while telemetry confidence < 30% (feature-flag controlled). PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1167 (safety-latch), https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/10423 (revert)
- Medium-term: Add dedupe-by-hash in ingestion pipeline and a watermark-based sample-consistency check to detect duplicate/partial merges. Work tracked in this ticket.
- Long-term: Strengthen autoscaler signal processing: add allocator-crosscheck (verify observed per-slot token rates against allocator table before scale-down) + outlier detection for sudden negative deltas in utilization.

Rollout plan for the permanent fix:
1) Merge telemetry dedupe + sample-consistency (canary 1% of ingestion shards) — ETA 2026-03-17.
2) Canary autoscaler allocator-crosscheck in a single AZ (us-west-2b) with additional telemetry instrumentation — ETA 2026-03-20.
3) Gradual ramp to full AZ coverage with feature-flag off by default until 2 weeks of stable telemetry — target completion 2026-04-04.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for window key normalization and dedupe hash function (telemetry repo).
- Integration test harness simulating dual-shard replay added to telemetry/test/harness (see runbook link).
- Autoscaler simulator extended with a reversible workload generator to validate safety-latch behavior under noisy metrics.

Stakeholders and communication:
- On-call: Marco Li (primary), backup: Deepa Rao
- PM: Elena Gomez (customer comms and SLA reconciliation)
- Support: Luis Mendes (customer updates)
- Notified: Execs and Sales for impacted accounts on 2026-03-08 morning digest

Follow-ups (postmortem action items):
- (Action 1) Instrument telemetry pipeline to emit dedupe-confidence metric (owner: telemetry eng, estimate: 3) — due 2026-03-21
- (Action 2) Add autoscaler allocator-crosscheck and unit/integration tests (owner: autoscaler team, estimate: 5) — due 2026-03-28
- (Action 3) Improve runbook automation: automated freeze of scale-down when ingestion confidence metric < threshold (owner: SRE, estimate: 2) — due 2026-03-19
- (Action 4) Customer SLA reconciliation and credits where applicable (owner: customer success, estimate: 1) — due 2026-03-15

References and artifacts:
- Incident timeline doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2026-03-telemetry-stitching
- Telemetry revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/10423
- Autoscaler safety latch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1167
- Autoscaler simulator harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/tree/main/simulator
- Support tickets: internal tracker link https://support.redwood.ai/tickets?query=9871,9900,9924

Notes and trade-offs considered:
- We deprecated a strict reliance on shard_id because it carried noisy proxy labels; the intent was correct (canonicalization) but the implementation removed a necessary dedupe constraint. The longer-term solution is to canonicalize while preserving an ingestion-unique id for dedupe.
- We opted for a quick revert + safety latch rather than a complex partial rollback across shards to minimize customer impact. This trades potential short-term conservatism (slightly higher cost due to retained headroom) against longer customer downtime and escalations.

Current next steps (this ticket):
- Complete telemetry dedupe implementation (owner: telemetry) and run 1% canary — due 2026-03-17.
- Implement autoscaler allocator-crosscheck (owner: autoscaler) and run integration tests — due 2026-03-20.
- Postmortem write-up and customer-facing summary — due 2026-03-16.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry ingestion dedupe prevents duplicated window samples in >= 99.9% of canary shard runs
Autoscaler refrains from performing scale-down when allocator-crosscheck fails or dedupe-confidence < configured threshold
No new customer-visible reserved-pool capacity shortfalls in canary AZ for 72h after rollout
Runbook automation triggers freeze of scale-down in presence of low ingestion confidence
